status_summary: On 2026-06-23 HHS's Office of Population Affairs posted a funding opportunity of an estimated 63.4 million dollars to replicate effective Teen Pregnancy Prevention programs, expecting sexual risk avoidance education and promotion of delayed sexual initiation, calling for advance parent notice and opt-out, and setting program eligibility criteria, and on 2026-06-26 HHS terminated 53 of 67 grants, about 68 million dollars, citing misalignment with agency priorities. On 2026-08-19 Judge Christopher R. Cooper (D.D.C., Hennepin County v. HHS, No. 1:26-cv-2460, ECF 33) preliminarily enjoined HHS from implementing its 2026 Teen Pregnancy Prevention policy, including the FY2026 funding notices, finding the policy likely arbitrary and capricious, while declining to reinstate the terminated grants. A joint status report of 2026-09-01 reported no program updates from HHS and did not mention an appeal, and no awards under the 2026 notices were found. The stage is blocked because the instrument that redirected the program is enjoined, while the terminations remain in place.

timeline.event: Office of Population Affairs posts the Replicating Effective Teen Pregnancy Prevention Programs funding opportunity (63.4 million dollars, about 52 awards), requiring sexual risk avoidance education and parent notice and opt-out.

Judge Christopher R. Cooper (D.D.C., Hennepin County, Minnesota v. HHS, No. 1:26-cv-2460, ECF 33) grants in part and denies in part a motion for a preliminary injunction, enjoining HHS until a merits ruling from implementing its 2026 policy for the Teen Pregnancy Prevention program to the extent consistent with the memorandum opinion, which finds the policy likely arbitrary and capricious, treats the FY2026 funding notices as final agency action and declines interim reinstatement of terminated grants; the order states that it is appealable.

title: Redirect the Teen Pregnancy Prevention program toward sexual risk avoidance
uncertainties: The order does not state whether the injunction is limited to the plaintiffs; the memorandum opinion's operative portion was not fully visible, though the joint status report describes the injunction as barring implementation of the FY2026 notices. The terminations rest on news reports; the termination letters were not read. Whether HHS reissued notices, made any awards or let FY2026 funds lapse after 2026-09-01 was not found: the OPA award announcements page lists nothing after January 2025, and the replication opportunity on simpler.grants.gov shows as archived on 2026-09-01. No appeal was found in the sources read; the joint status report of 2026-09-01 does not mention one. On 2026-09-24 the plaintiffs moved for an emergency status conference (Dkt. 42), stating that HHS had awarded additional funds to remaining Tier 2 grantees late on 2026-09-23 and might award remaining FY2026 Tier 1 funds through a single contract around 2026-09-29; the defendants opposed and say the funds will be spent consistent with the injunction. That motion is a party filing, and no court ruling on it, or on the plaintiffs' 2026-09-02 motion to hold funds, was found. The 53-of-67 termination count rests on news reporting; the memorandum opinion describes nearly all of the 2023 to 2028 cohort as terminated. The joint status report is a party filing and is cited as a source rather than listed as a court action. PREP and funding parity were not examined.
